title: Company-wide policies and process documentation
author: Avery Patel
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel, and commonly used internal templates. It is intended as the single reference for employees and managers to ensure consistent, auditable, and compliant operations across teams.

Scope

Applies to: all Redwood employees, contractors, and third-party vendors who access company systems or represent Redwood in vendor, procurement, or travel activities.

Policies and procedure owners

- People Ops: primary owner for access, travel, and internal templates.
- Engineering Security: co-owner for privileged access, RBAC, and change management for infra and services.
- Finance & Legal: owner for procurement, vendor contracts, expense policy, and compliance.
- IT/Platform: operational owner for provisioning, device management, and system inventory.

1) Access and permissions

Goal: Ensure least privilege, traceability of access, and timely revocation.

Key principles:
- Least privilege by default. Access is granted for defined roles and reviewed periodically.
- Just-in-time (JIT) access for high-privilege operations where supported.
- Two-person approval for access to production systems.
- All access requests must have an explicit business justification and an expiration date.

Roles and definitions:
- Employee: standard accounts (email, Slack, SSO).
- Privileged Operator: sandbox and staging ops with elevated rights. Requires manager + security approval.
- Production Operator: production console, deployment, and DBA-level access. Requires manager + security + infra lead approval.

Requesting access (step-by-step):
1. Submit request via Access Request form (Confluence template: "access-request-template").
2. Provide role, justification, scope, and required duration.
3. Manager reviews and approves; Security team performs risk review for privileged requests.
4. IT/Platform provisions or schedules JIT access.
5. Access is recorded in the central Access Registry (IT asset inventory).

Access review and revocation:
- Quarterly access reviews by team managers; audit by Security annually.
- Immediate revocation required when an employee leaves or switches to a role that no longer requires access. Offboarding checklist triggers automated deprovisioning.

Authentication and MFA:
- SSO (Okta) is enforced for all company systems.
- MFA required for all accounts; hardware MFA recommended for privileged operators.

2) Change management (infra, service, and config changes)

Purpose: Prevent unintended outages and ensure controlled rollouts. Applies to infra, runtime, deployment pipelines, critical configs, and schema migrations.

Change classification:
- Standard: pre-approved low-risk changes (routine config tweaks, minor package updates).
- Planned: scheduled changes with a rollback plan (deployments, DB migrations).
- Emergency: unplanned fixes to restore service or security; require post-facto approval and postmortem.

Pre-change checklist for Planned changes:
- Owner and rollback owner identified.
- Impact assessment and blast radius documented.
- Backout/rollback plan and automated rollback hooks configured in CI/CD.
- Runbook updated if behavior will change.
- Stakeholder notification: oncall, product, and affected customers (if applicable).

Approval flow:
1. Create a change request (Change Management form).
2. Attach runbooks, test results, and rollout plan.
3. For Standard changes, notify approvers via the standard-change Slack channel; automated approvals apply.
4. For Planned changes, obtain approvals: manager, service owner, and change advisory board (CAB) for high-impact items.
5. Schedule maintenance windows where required; post status updates to Status Page.

Emergency change process:
- Execute emergency fix with minimum required approvals (oncall + service owner).
- Create an emergency change ticket within 24 hours and attach evidence.
- Conduct a postmortem within 7 business days for any emergency change with service impact.

Change window and SLO impact:
- Avoid non-critical planned changes during high-traffic windows (Mon–Fri 09:00–18:00 PT).
- Any change expected to impact availability >0.1% or latency >20% during the SLO period must be escalated to CAB.

3) Data management

Objective: Protect customer and company data, ensure correct retention, and provide guidance on labeling, storage, and sharing.

Data classification levels:
- Public: information safe to publish externally.
- Internal: company-internal operational data.
- Restricted: customer-identifiable data or regulated information.
- Confidential: security-sensitive or legal materials.

Data handling rules:
- Restricted and Confidential data must be stored in approved systems with encryption at rest and in transit (e.g., S3 with SSE-KMS, RDS with TLS).
- Minimum necessary access: follow role-based access.
- No restricted data in personal accounts or unmanaged devices.
- Pseudonymize or redact customer identifiers where feasible for analytics or evals.

Retention and deletion:
- Standard retention for logs: 90 days hot, 365 days cold (default). Custom retention requires Data Steward approval.
- Deletion requests and data subject requests handled by Legal + Data Stewards via the Data Request form.

Backups and DR:
- Daily backups for critical databases; weekly snapshots for analytics stores. Restore drills at least twice per year.

Data inventory and ownership:
- Every dataset must have an assigned Data Steward and owner listed in the Data Inventory spreadsheet.
- Data inventory review: quarterly.

4) Procurement and expenses

Objective: Ensure controls for company spend, timely approvals, and consistent vendor onboarding.

Thresholds and approval matrix:
- < $1,000: Team lead approval.
- $1,000 – $10,000: Manager + Finance approval.
- $10,000 – $100,000: Director + Finance approval and Legal review for contracts.
- > $100,000: VP-level approval + Legal and Procurement involvement.

Procurement process (summary):
1. Complete Procurement Request form with business justification and budget code.
2. Finance reviews budget and approves based on thresholds.
3. For vendor relationships, Legal reviews contract terms and security questionnaires.
4. Finance issues PO or approves card use.

Corporate card & expense policy:
- Employees with recurring vendor needs may be allocated a corporate card (issued by Finance).
- Expense reports submitted within 30 days of expenditure. Late submissions may be rejected.
- Receipts required for all expenses > $25.
- Travel and hospitality limits: see Travel section below.

5) Vendor management and security review

Vendor lifecycle:
- Assess -> Onboard -> Monitor -> Offboard.

Required pre-onboarding checks:
- Security questionnaire (vendor-vetting-form).
- Legal review of contract and DPA for vendors handling Restricted or Confidential data.
- Insurance and SOC/ISO evidence where appropriate.

Ongoing monitoring:
- Quarterly performance and security reviews for strategic vendors.
- SLA and billing reconciliation monthly for major vendors.

Termination and offboarding:
- Ensure data return/destruction clauses are enforced.
- Revoke access and collect any issued assets.
- Maintain an offboarding record in Vendor Registry.

6) Travel policy

Purpose: Provide safe, cost-effective travel while meeting business needs.

Booking and approval:
- All business travel requires pre-approval via the Travel Request form.
- Approval hierarchy: Manager -> Finance for trips > $2,000 or international travel; VP for extended travel (>14 days).

Airfare and lodging guidance:
- Economy or premium economy for flights under 6 hours. Business class for flights longer than 6 hours requires VP approval.
- Hotels should be mid-tier business class near the meeting location. Use preferred vendor list where available.

Per diems and meals:
- Daily meal allowance: $75 domestic, $120 international. Exceptions require manager approval.

Safety and insurance:
- Company travel insurance covers medical and evacuation for approved trips. Register international trips with People Ops.

Expense reporting:
- Submit itemized receipts within 30 days. Use the Expense Report template.

7) Internal templates and forms (quick list)

- access-request-template (Access Request)
- change-management-request (Change Request)
- data-request-form (Data Subject/Deletion)
- procurement-request-template (Procurement)
- vendor-security-questionnaire (Vendor Onboarding)
- travel-request-template (Travel Approval)
- expense-report-template (Expense Submission)

8) Audit, training, and compliance

- Annual mandatory training: Security Basics, Data Handling, and Expense Policy.
- Quarterly spot audits for access and vendor compliance by Finance & Security.
- Non-compliance consequences: corrective coaching, access restrictions, or disciplinary action per People Ops policy.

9) Escalations and contacts

- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.ai
- Finance: finance@redwood.ai
- Legal: legal@redwood.ai
- Security: security@redwood.ai
- IT/Platform: it-platform@redwood.ai

Appendices

Appendix A — Change request checklist (table)

| Item | Required? | Owner | Notes |
|------|-----------|-------|-------|
| Runbook attached | Yes | Change owner | Include rollback steps |
| Impact assessment | Yes | Change owner | Include expected SLO impact |
| Test evidence | Yes for Planned | CI owner | Automated tests preferred |
| Stakeholder notification | Yes | Change owner | Slack + Status Page if customer-facing |

Appendix B — Procurement quick matrix (table)

| Amount | Approval required | Additional steps |
|--------|-------------------|------------------|
| <$1,000 | Team lead | Use team budget code |
| $1,000–$10,000 | Manager + Finance | Verify vendor status |
| $10,000–$100,000 | Director + Finance + Legal | Security questionnaire + contract |
| >$100,000 | VP + Legal + Procurement | Exec sponsor + board notification if strategic |

How to use this document

- Follow the templates linked above for any request.
- When in doubt, contact the owner listed in each section.
- This document will be reviewed annually by People Ops, Finance, and Security.
